revision_table.in_short: The identity of the substance changes and a new substance forms.
revision_table.remember: Signs: change of state, colour, gas given off, temperature change

revision_table.in_short: The number of atoms of each element is the same on both sides.
Two or more substances combine to form a single product.
A single reactant breaks down into simpler products by heat, light or electricity.
Gain of oxygen (or loss of hydrogen) is oxidation; loss of oxygen (or gain of hydrogen) is reduction.

rows.a: A more reactive element replaces a less reactive one
rows.b: Ions are exchanged between two compounds

case_based.passage: A student heated ferrous sulphate crystals in a dry boiling tube. The green crystals turned colourless, then a brown solid was left behind and a gas with the smell of burning sulphur was given off.

questions.question: Why did the green colour disappear first?
questions.answer: The crystals lost their water of crystallisation.

questions.question: Write the balanced chemical equation and name the brown solid.
questions.answer:
- 2FeSO₄(s) → Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g)
- The brown solid is ferric oxide, Fe₂O₃.

points: Magnesium ribbon burns in air with a dazzling white flame and forms a white powder, magnesium oxide.
Remember to clean the ribbon with sandpaper first and to hold it with tongs, away from the eyes.
Zinc granules react with dilute sulphuric acid in a conical flask; hydrogen gas is given off.
Be able to label: cork, glass tube, conical flask, dilute sulphuric acid, zinc granules.
Calcium oxide (quick lime) reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime and releases heat: a combination reaction that is exothermic.
